title: Leicester appoint Gary Rowett as new manager
content:
Leicester City have confirmed the appointment of Gary Rowett as their new manager.

The 51-year-old has signed a contract until the end of the season and replaces Marti Cifuentes, who was sacked last month after a run of just two wins in eight league games.

Rowett, a former right-back who made 57 appearances for Leicester between 2000 and 2002, last managed Oxford United. He guided the Championship side to safety in the 2024-25 season, finishing 17th, but was dismissed in December with the club 22nd in the table.

He has managed more than 400 games in the second tier across spells with Burton Albion, Birmingham City, Derby County, Stoke City, Millwall and Oxford.

“It’s very clear to us all what needs to be achieved between now and the end of the season and the work begins immediately,” Rowett said after being appointed. “I’m looking forward to building connections with the players, with the staff at the club and with the fans – all of which will be vital to helping us secure the results we need.”

Leicester chairman Aiyawatt Srivaddhanaprabha added: “Gary is a manager with deep knowledge of the Championship and experience of the situation we now face in these final 14 games of the season – a fight for survival in the division. It is a task on which the entire club is focused, and we will provide Gary with every support to help us find the solutions we need.”

Rowett takes over Leicester with the club in the relegation zone. Earlier this month, Leicester were given a six-point deduction for breaching the English Football League’s profit and sustainability rules (PSR), with the sanction being handed down by an independent commission. A Premier League statement explained the commission had determined that the club had breached the PSR threshold by £20.8million ($28.2m) over the three-year assessment period.

Callum Davidson has joined the club as an assistant manager under Rowett. First team coach Andy King, who took interim charge of the side after Cifuentes’ departure and lost all four games, will remain at the club as part of the coaching staff.

Rowett’s first game in charge will be a visit to Stoke on Saturday.

It has been over three weeks since Leicester sacked Cifuentes with their Championship status hanging in the balance.

Now, finally, they have appointed his successor, former Leicester defender Rowett, initially on a short-term contract.

There clearly wasn’t a succession plan at Leicester when inconsistent performances and, more importantly, results, started to drift away from Cifuentes.

Rowett was one of the candidates they spoke to early on but the delay in his appointment, considering he was instantly available after being sacked by Oxford on December 23, would suggest the hierarchy hoped interim King could halt their slide.

That was unfair on King, a club legend having won three divisional titles as a player, and who was just starting his coaching journey at 37.

Leicester have been hit with a six-point deduction for breaching profit and sustainability rules during their last season in the Championship in 2023-24, when they won the  title.

They now find themselves battling to avoid successive relegations and a drop into League One for only the second time in their history.

Rowett, who has been apppointed until the end of the season, was able to keep Oxford in the Championship last season, but two seasons ago failed to keep Birmingham City in the second tier after being given a similar assignment.

With Leicester facing mounting issues off the pitch and a fan protest arranged for their next home game against Norwich City, Rowett is taking on a huge challenge.
